sentences.form: Numa ya pinudaqu iza kmalawa sa lhalhaushin, marutaw a lhalhaushin.
sentences.translation: After the Pudaqu festival (for sowing the hill rice) we made swings, tall swings.

sentences.form: Numa sa caw mashtay iza mukaktun iza malhuiza sa lhqaribush a pazay, numa mu-lhckiz sa caw musun musaháy yanan sa lhalhaushin.
sentences.translation: When everyone was finished planting the hill rice they would all come together at the swings.

sentences.form: Muriut mashtay kmacu sa lhqaribush a sinapuk a lhqaribush a aqtalha, numa musún iutu mashtay kman aqtalha, numa ya itia sa pinigqilha tu caw a qilha ansunin isaháy yanan lhalhaushin miqilha.
sentences.translation: Everyone brought game and crowded together to eat the meat, and if someone brought home-made wine they gathered at the swings to drink.

sentences.form: Yanan sa lhmaushin yanan sa miqilha matigqaran iutu, mapatigquyash.
sentences.translation: Some would be swinging, others would be drinking and making merry and singing.

sentences.form: Numa sa parhaway ya niwan tu minara sa binanau'az iutu ya matqal sa a min mita wa binanau'az.
sentences.translation: Then the young men who hadn't yet chosen a wife would mark the woman they wanted to marry.

sentences.form: Numa sa dadú qazí `Maniun parhaway ya tima sa kadaduun ihu a binanau'az shunasaháy ihu lhalhaushin palhaushin'.
sentences.translation: The chief said `You young men, whoever you find suitable as a wife, pull her over to the swing and make her swing with you.

sentences.form: `Ya muapaw lhmaushin mihu iza wa a minbinanau'az'.
sentences.translation: If she is seen to swing with you she will become your wife'.

sentences.form: Numa sa suma macuaw ya itia sa shinuruz mashtay kmay pakpak matigqaran.
sentences.translation: And if someone was pulled (to the swing) everyone really clapped and celebrated.

sentences.form: Kahiwan tata wa taun a caw latusha sa parhaway, numa sa ama ina miaqawan itia.
sentences.translation: Once upon a time there were two brothers who still lived under the same roof with their parents.

sentences.form: Macuaw latusha wa minlhafut mapaqaqitan mashtay iza sa izaháy a parhaway minara sa binanau'az, numa mashtay iza yanan sa azazak.
sentences.translation: They got along well, and were married and had children.

sentences.form: Numa tu ikahin a makashiqca sa taun, numa sa izaháy a parhaway kmilhim izaháy a kawi a mintaun.
sentences.translation: After awhile they decided to build an extension on their house, so they went to search for wood to make it.

sentences.form: Mutusi tanasaya kan tatusha mriqaz sa kawi, numa tu itia sa riniqazan cicu a kawi lhiklhikin cicu puntunuq
sentences.translation: The two of them went up into the mountains and spotted a tree, and then they sawed it until it toppled to the ground.

sentences.form: Lhintutunin cicu, numa simaq iza kmacu iza maquliush a lhalhiklhik, numa sa izaháy a kawi a lhindazumdumin a migqrus, a mimpinazim.
sentences.translation: After that they cut the log into cross sections, and the next day they brought a long saw and cut the sections lengthwise to make house posts and walls.

sentences.form: Numa izaháy a latusha wa minlhafut mimpiza wa qali miaqay mutusi tanasaya lhmiklhik sa a mintaun a kawi.
sentences.translation: For several days the two brothers made frequent trips up the mountain, sawing away at the tree which was to become their house.

sentences.form: Numa ya mutusi tanasaya lhmiklhik izaháy a kawi a makacu sa pinuqafay, numa tu saqazi iza kman iza sa pinuqafay.
sentences.translation: When they went up the mountain to work they took their lunch basket, and at noon they would eat from it.

sentences.form: Numa sa izaháy a mintaun a kawi pilhalhilhin caycuy lhmiklhik, numa tu piza iza wa qali lhiniklhikan, numa sa izaháy a kawi lhiniklhik caycuy antu ukaktunin caycuy lhmiklhik, numa pagqa caycuy kunsaqazi.
sentences.translation: They stood the logs for making the house upright to saw them, and after some days of sawing without completing the work they stopped to eat lunch.

sentences.form: Numa izaháy a kawi lhiniklhik caycuy pasizan cicu sa izaháy lhiniklhikan a saran, kanuniza ya antu pasizan, niza tu maqitan ya lhiklhikin.
sentences.translation: Meanwhile they propped open the sawed log with a wedge, since otherwise it would close up.

sentences.form: Numa caycuy tu kminsaqazi kman isaháy caycuy shirshir mapakalhus uan.
sentences.translation: Then after they ate they took a nap at the side of the log.

sentences.form: Numa tu itiza sa izaháy manasha wa rucun musaháy yanan caycuy lhiniklhik a kawi, matigqaran caycuy iutu mriqaz lhiniklhik caycuy a kawi, iutu cicu matinhina sa lhalhiklhik.
sentences.translation: As they napped a troupe of monkeys arrived at the place they had been sawing wood, and became fascinated at the sight of the wood that had been sawed, and so they started to play with the saw.'

sentences.form: Numa sa latusha wa minlhafut miaqawan malhus, numa sa izaháy a rucun manshaish caycuy iutu latusha mapashashuruz lhmiklhik sa kawi migqaray sa latusha malhus, numa sa rucun migqaray matinhina sa lhalhiklhik.
sentences.translation: As the two brothers dozed the monkeys took turns pushing the saw and continued to play with it.

sentences.form: Numa sa tata wa rucun izaháy pinasiz izaháy a kawi shururun cicu, numa sa rucun a fatu qpitin izaháy a kawi.
sentences.translation: Then one of the monkeys pulled the wedge from the wood and the log snapped shut on his testicles.

sentences.form: Numa izaháy a rucun macuaw makaqiaqia, numa sa suma wa rucun muiutu a mashuzáy, minshuz qumpit rucun a fatu.
sentences.translation: He let out a terrific howl and kept screeching, so some of the other monkeys went to free him, but in their efforts to help they only squeezed his testicles harder.

sentences.form: Numa sa izaháy latusha wa minlhafut pansaqazi mimpulhiz maqa sa izaháy a rucun qpitin sa kawi cicu sa kawi cicu a fatu, numa latusha minlhafut malalia makunasay mriqaz caycuy a lhiniklhik a kawi.
sentences.translation: The brothers awoke from their afternoon nap with the commotion of the monkeys, and they ran to see the log they had been sawing.

sentences.form: Numa izaháy a rucun macuaw makaqiaqia, numa sakpin latusha wa minlhafut, numa rucun a rima qucqucan latusha wa minlhafut.
sentences.translation: The monkey who was pinched was howling pathetically and the two brothers caught him and tied his arms.

sentences.form: Muqay iza suma wa rucun isaháy shirshir mriqariqaz izah'ay qucqucan a rucun.
sentences.translation: Meanwhile some of the monkeys on the side just watched the monkey that was tied.

sentences.form: Numa tu tanlhuan iza latusha wa minlhafut pagqa iza lhmiklhik a musha iza mutaun, numa sa rucun apapan caycuy a kay pacayin caycuy ya mutaun iza.
sentences.translation: That evening the brothers took a break from sawing to go home, carrying the monkey there to kill it.

sentences.form: Numa tu musha iza caycuy mu-lhckiz izaháy suma wa rucun yanan sa huqi uan a rucun kman tup izaháy latusha wa minlhafut, mashtay izaháy rucun mapatincanit kman tup.
sentences.translation: But all of the monkeys, even the babies, followed them weeping.

sentences.form: Numa sa izaháy latusha wa minlhafut izaháy shashuazi mzai `Ata tu sakpí, minu sa rucun mapatincanit'.
sentences.translation: So the younger brother said `Don't keep it captive, because all the monkeys are crying'.

sentences.form: Izaháy cicu a shashuazi, numa sa izaháy tanatuqash `Antu shmirua', numa latusha mapaimbuqnur.
sentences.translation: The elder brother said `I don't agree with you', and the two of them got angry with one another.

sentences.form: Numa sa izaháy shashuazi madaidaiz izaháy rucun, maqa dai kman tup caycuy mapatincanit.
sentences.translation: But the younger brother felt compassion for the monkeys because they were following them and all weeping together.

sentences.form: Numa uan izaháy shashuazi mimbuqnur `Shrakin cicu sa izaháy a qinucquc, pusha cicu izaháy a rucun'.
sentences.translation: He became angry and demanded `Untie the monkey and let him go!'.

sentences.form: Numa tu shaunatuan iza fuifuilh cicu a ama masa ina mzai `Ata tu sakpí, azuan miazay itan caw maní tatál sa shaqish'.
sentences.translation: When they arrived home they told the story to their parents, who said `Don't capture them; they are like us humans, with the same kind of face.'

sentences.form: Numa tu taqali iza muqca caycuy mutanautu a malhiklhik izaháy a kawi, numa sa izaháy yanan caycuy lhmiklhik a pruq, manasha sa izaháy funfun, pinusun izaháy a rucun a pansha sa izaháy latusha wa minlhafut iutu lhimiklhik sa kawi.
sentences.translation: Two days later they went back again to saw wood, and in the place where they were sawing they saw a lot of fruits which had been gathered by the monkeys to give as gifts to the brothers who had been sawing wood there.

words.note: the fruit of the tree Castanopsis indica.

sentences.form: Numa riqazan izaháy latusha wa minlhafut, zain `Numa sa izaháy kuntumbuz?'
sentences.translation: When the brothers saw it they exclaimed `What is that pile?'.

sentences.form: Pasarima cicu mribuq azaz dai funfun, numa sa izaháy wa minlhafut mapazazáy mzai `Tu rucun painan inlhay itan'.
sentences.translation: Then they ran their hands through the fruits, and they spoke to one another, saying `Perhaps they were given to us by the monkeys'.

sentences.form: Macuaw latusha mapatigqaran mriqaz izaháy a funfun.
sentences.translation: The two of them really rejoiced to see so many fruits.

sentences.form: Numa tu tanlhuan iza apapan caycuy izaháy a funfun manataun.
sentences.translation: That night they took the fruits home.

sentences.form: Numa tu shaunataun iza mashtay cicu a ama masa ina mzai `Manu a inlhay a funfun?'
sentences.translation: When they arrived their parents asked them `Who gave you the fruits?'.

sentences.form: Numa fuifuilhan latusha wa minlhafut mzai `Tu rucun a inlhay pisain cicu yanan yamin lhiklhik sa kawi piasunin cicu'.
sentences.translation: The brothers told them `They were given to us by the monkeys in the place where we were sawing wood'.

sentences.form: Numa sa cicu a ama masa ina tmusuq mzai `Ata ita tu kakan rucun a bunlhaz, parshian ya kman'.
sentences.translation: Then their parents lectured them, saying `We should not eat the flesh of monkeys, it is taboo to eat'.

texts.title: The Monkeys Who Were Sawing Wood

sentences.form: Yamin ya isáy makashpashpat furaz nam a caw a Lus'an.
sentences.translation: In the eighth month we Thao celebrate the New Year.

sentences.form: Numa isaháy musuy yamin zain Raushian.
sentences.translation: At that time we go to the person called Raushian.

sentences.form: Cicu sa tmatitish, numa yanan shishí mulalu, numa mulhckiz yamin, tuqatuqash, parhaway, azazak musúy Raushian titishan, maqa yamin Lus'an.
sentences.translation: He performs a (ceremonial) cleansing, then a shaman calls up the ancestors and all of us, old, young, and children go to Raushian to be purified because it is our New Year.

sentences.form: Numa malhkakca ya pashaila ya ani.
sentences.translation: Then we discuss whether to hold the ceremonial dance or not.

sentences.form: Ya itia pariqaz isisuaiza ya shmaila, pariqaz a masashdu, isisuaiza ya shmaila.
sentences.translation: If there is an overseer who agrees that we should dance, we will dance then.

sentences.form: Numa ya itia pariqaz maní a makalawa tuza, numa a paruan azazak nipin a ma'aruz'uz, makaligkin.
sentences.translation: Likewise, if there is an overseer for making rice eels and for the ceremonial tooth extraction of the adolescents (we do it) so they will be vigorous and healthy.

sentences.form: Kmalawan maní hanán
sentences.translation: And then we also make a temporary temple to host the ancestral spirits.

sentences.form: Tu kahiwan inay Zintun numa Shtafari mapakiqualh numa sa Shtafari azaz Shlilitun.
sentences.translation: In former times from Sun-Moon Lake as far as Tou-she there was no one here but the `Little People'.

sentences.form: Numa sa Shlilitun miaqay munanay Zintun kmay na taun inay a caw.
sentences.translation: Some of the Little People often came to Sun-Moon Lake to raid the houses of the Thao.

sentences.form: Numa sa inay a caw minriri masaháy Shlilitun mapacay.
sentences.translation: So the Thao retaliated and killed them.

sentences.form: Macuaw Shlilitun miku riway sa inay Zintun a pruq maqa sa inay Zintun maqitan yanan a pruq maqa sa caw makaligkin.
sentences.translation: Many Little People wanted to occupy Sun-Moon Lake because it is such a fine place and the Thao prospered there.

sentences.form: Numa sa Shlilitun miku qalaw sa inay Zintun.
sentences.translation: The Little People wanted to take away this land.

sentences.form: Numa tu migqaray iza sa Shlilitun mapacay masa inay Zintun a caw, numa antu pikbzaw inay sa Zintun a caw.
sentences.translation: Eventually the Little People fought with the inhabitants of Sun-Moon Lake, but they couldn't defeat them.

sentences.form: Numa tu isisuaiza kmari sa Shtafari a hudun a pugqalhiwan caycuy sazum inay Zintun.
sentences.translation: So they dug through Mt. Shtafari to drain the water out of Sun-Moon Lake.

sentences.form: Numa a pugqalhiwan cicu sa inay a Zintun a wazaqan, a punatusin cicu sa Shtafari sa inay a sazum a miazáy inay Zintun yanan maní wazaqan.
sentences.translation: They were going to drain the water from Sun-Moon Lake to Tou-she to make a similar lake there.

sentences.form: Numa sa Shlilitun macuaw makarishkish mapa sa pruq a piazain caycuy miazáy sa Lalu.
sentences.translation: The Little People worked hard carrying earth to make something like Lalu Island.

sentences.form: Numa riqazan lhqananay Zintun a caw kmari sa izáy Tibabu mashnatusi Shtafari a hudun.
sentences.translation: The people living at Sun-Moon Lake saw them digging at Tibabu through Mt. Shtafari.

sentences.form: Isisuaiza tu mapacay masaháy Shlilitun, mapacay, mabuqnur lhqananay Zintun a caw karin caycuy izáy Tibabu a pugqalhiwan caycuy inay Zintun.
sentences.translation: As a result they came to blows with the Little People (because) the inhabitants of Sun-Moon Lake were angry that the Little People had dug out Tibabu to drain their lake.

sentences.form: Numa tu mapacay iza antu matunaw sa Shlilitun, minlawashwash sa Shlilitun.
sentences.translation: They fought, and the Little People were defeated and scattered far and wide.

sentences.form: Numa sa Shtafari a pruq riwazin lhqananay Zintun a caw, numa zain lhqananay Zintun a caw Shtafari.
sentences.translation: Then Tou-she was occupied by the people of Sun-Moon Lake, and they called it Shtafari.

sentences.form: Numa sa caw mutusi Shtafari sa suma pimbuhat, pintaun itantu iza Shtafari kataun.
sentences.translation: So some of the Thao went to Tou-she to farm and build houses to make Tou-she their home.

texts.title: The Little People and the Lake

sentences.form: Yamin igkahiwan nam a tanatuqash initusi zain cuini Kagi a pruq.
sentences.source_form_raw: Yamin (tu) igkahiwan nam a tanatuqash initusi zain cuini Kagi a pruq.
sentences.translation: Long ago our ancestors lived in the place that is now called Chia-yi.

sentences.form: Yamin tu igkahiwan nam a tanatuqash initusi zain cuini Kagi a pruq.
sentences.source_form_raw: Yamin (tu) igkahiwan nam a tanatuqash initusi zain cuini Kagi a pruq.
sentences.translation: Long ago our ancestors lived in the place that is now called Chia-yi.

sentences.form: Turu iza wa shaba, yanan tu mashpatiz a qamishan shaunacuini, numa yamin macuaw manasha sa caw.
sentences.translation: Three hundred and forty years ago, we were a numerous people gathered in that place.

sentences.form: Macuaw maqitan dai itantu miasun, mashtay mapapaqitan, numa dai ya mubuhat minshashauluk, mashtay dai mapapaqitan mubuhat.
sentences.translation: Everyone got along well, working cooperatively, and farming together in harmony.

sentences.form: Numa ya muribush sa parhaway, itia matiqtu sa lhqaribush, mashtay dai musun, kman sa lhqaribush, masa a azazak, mashtay kalushan lhqaribush a bunlhaz.
sentences.translation: When the young men went out to trap game everyone was invited to eat the game they caught, even the children, everyone was given a share in the distribution of meat.

sentences.form: Numa tu itiza sa minakatusi Toalu munay mriway nam a pruq.
sentences.translation: Then people who wanted to occupy this land arrived from China.

sentences.form: Kmay na taun, numa tu migqaray iza ani yamin tu matunaw, numa yamin antu matunaw, numa sa caw shugkash, tunatusi zain cuini Alisan a pruq.
sentences.translation: They destroyed our homes, and eventually we lost, so the people were afraid, and fled to the place now called Mt. Ali.

sentences.form: Numa tu a muqca iza a Lus'an, numa yamin parhaway muqca iza muribush, maqa a Lus'an mashtay sa caw kmilhim sa lhqaribush a pakan sa caw ya a Lus'an.
sentences.translation: The New Year was approaching so our youth went out to hunt again, because at New Years all the Thao search for game to feed the people at the New Year festival.

sentences.form: Numa ya a Lus'an mashtay musun shmaila matigqaran a azazak.
sentences.translation: At the New Year everyone gathered to rejoice with the children.

sentences.form: Mashtay musun masa tanatuqash.
sentences.translation: Everyone came together, even the old people.

sentences.form: Mashtay muapaw mimparaw maqaran Lus'an.
sentences.translation: Everyone came out and leaped with joy in celebration of the New Year.

sentences.form: Numa tu muqca iza pugkawash, miazicu muqca iza maní muribush, mashtay parhaway puqafay afu, pinarbu a buna pisain lhalhahi, mashtay mapa masa futulh, funush, shinabun'an, mashtay kmacu a musha iza muribush.
sentences.translation: So before the next year arrived they went out hunting, all the young people carrying baskets of rice on their backs, with roasted sweet potatoes put in their net bags, everyone carried bows, knives and spears to go out hunting.

sentences.form: Numa sa suma shmushul sa atu a muribush, numa tu musay iza hudun pusha sa atu muhiaw, ugqtuan lhqaribush a qnuan, numa sa izahay atu qmaqutilh lh.a.q.
sentences.translation: Some took their dogs to go hunting, and they went to the mountains urging the dogs on to discover game, and then the dogs began to pursue a deer.

sentences.form: Numa tu qmaqutilh iza lh.a.q. miaqay sa parhaway kman tutup sa atu.
sentences.translation: And so the young people followed their dogs relentlessly in pursuit of the deer.

sentences.form: Antu mimpanu sa parhaway miaqay kman tutúp sa atu.
sentences.translation: The young people didn't grow tired, but kept following their dogs.

sentences.form: Tanlhuan iza, lh.a.q. antu kmihazish.
sentences.translation: Evening came and the deer hadn't gotten far.

sentences.form: Numas parhaway maqas izáy lh.a.q. antu miaqay iqualh, numa tu mahumhum iza paqai qmaqutilh mahumhum iza.
sentences.translation: The young people wanted to quit because it was already dark and the deer was not at hand.

sentences.form: Yanan sa parhaway mzai `Ata tu paqai, iaqay qmaqutilh'.
sentences.translation: But one youth said `Don't give up — keep up the chase.

sentences.form: Numa tu mahumhum iza isáy a ribush malhus, mayaw ya mutaun uka sa lhqaribush sinapuk'.
sentences.translation: Since it is dark already let's sleep in the forest; we would be ashamed to go home without catching the deer.'

sentences.form: Numa tu malhias iza muqca sa atu puribush, minu miazazáy maní tilha wa lh.a.q. qaqutilhin sa atu, numa tu qmaqutilh iza, makunanáy tanadu.
sentences.translation: When daylight came the dogs returned to the forest to pursue the deer they had been chasing the previous day, and then they veered to the right.

sentences.form: Miaqay isáy hudun migkakarunkun miazicu maníqali tanlhuan iza.
sentences.translation: They circled around the mountain repeatedly, and so day passed into evening again.

sentences.form: Numa sa parhaway mzai `Pagka uan, tanlhuan iza, utaun uan'.
sentences.translation: Then a youth said `Let's take a break, it's evening already, so let's go home'.

sentences.form: Suma mara sa a kanin, uka iza sa pinuqafay.
sentences.translation: Some got food, since there was no more in the carrying baskets.

sentences.form: Numa sa suma musha mutaun mara sa kanin, numa sa suma i sa ribush miacun.
sentences.translation: Some went home to get food and some slept overnight in the forest.

sentences.form: Simaq iza makakca, pusha sa atu qmaqutilh migqaray uan miazicu iza mialundunduz manaraus makunasáy waqrac a sazum, midaudauk mugkuruz.
sentences.translation: The next day they resumed the chase, sending the dogs in pursuit until eventually the deer made a beeline downhill into the river and kept still in hiding.

sentences.form: Numa sa atu mimbabuqbuq shmazik sa lh.a.q.
sentences.translation: Then the dogs got confused with the scent.

sentences.form: Numa tu tanlhuan iza muapaw iza lh.a.q. munsáy waqrac mialundunduz makunanáy zain tu Tumpú dai a pruq, numa makunanáy zain dai Aksa wa pruq, numa shaunanáy puzi dai a hudun, numa sa lh.a.q. munsáy puzi mrauz makunatusi magkaci.
sentences.translation: When evening came the deer appeared following the river straight to the place called Tumpú, then here to the place called Aksa before arriving at White Mountain, from where it swam to the other side.

sentences.form: Numa sa parhaway muqay iza mriqariqaz mufarit sa lh.a.q, miaqay sa parhaway ananaikin sa lhqaribush a qnuan.
sentences.translation: Then the young people watched the deer cross, and they greatly regretted losing it.

sentences.form: Numa sa atu makakca migqca qmaqutilh sa takic, muhiaw patiqtun sa takic, iutu iza kmackac sa takic.
sentences.translation: The dogs took up the chase again by changing their pursuit to a barking deer which was quickly caught and gutted.

sentences.form: Numa isay shirshir sazum parhaway shminaw sa takic a rumrum; minu iza manasha sa rusaw musun.
sentences.translation: Then by the edge of the water the young people washed the intestines of the barking deer and a great swarm of fish gathered there.

sentences.form: Minshkash a parhaway, numa sa parhaway mara sa funush, pasain funush tmala sa rusaw.
sentences.translation: The young people began to grow afraid so a youth fetched knives and they used them to chop up the fish.

sentences.form: Manasha sa paiqtuan, araran caycuy.
sentences.translation: Many were butchered and taken away.

sentences.form: Numa shiqalhiwan caycuy sa rusaw masa takic a bunlhaz.
sentences.translation: They then dried the fish and barking deer flesh.

sentences.form: Numa tu malhacas iza, mzai sa mashitantuqash, `Igqa uan maniun parhaway tu iahala kman sa rusaw, tihauta ya maqitankanin.
sentences.translation: Then, when they were cooked an elder said `Don't you young people eat the fish first, since I'm not sure if it's good to eat.

sentences.form: Yaku tanatuqash, manasha iza kamishan a kunhala kman, ya maqitan a mashtay parhaway kman.
sentences.translation: I, an elder who has seen many years, will eat it first to see if it is good for all of you young people to eat'.

sentences.form: Numa tu mahumhum isay hudun miacun.
sentences.translation: At sunset they stayed overnight on the mountain.

sentences.form: Numa sa parhaway iutu mapakalhus, numa tu mahumhum iza izáy mashitantuqash matiashaq dai mzai `Izáy mapuzipuzi lh.a.q. mimbinanau'az ifazan mapuzipuzi a hulus'.
sentences.translation: The young people all slept together there, and when it was dark the elder dreamt and said `The white deer there has changed to a woman dressed in white clothing'.

sentences.form: Fuilh izáy tanatuqash, mzai `Yaku sa kmacu maniun munay, yanan sa wazaqan, yanan sa qariw a pimbuhat'.
sentences.translation: Then (she) informed the elder `I am the one who brought you here to have a lake for your own and to have good lands for farming'.

sentences.form: Numa tu shashanu iza mimpulhiziza fuilh sa parhaway, mzai `Yaku lhuan matiashaq tata wa binanau'az ifazan mapuzipuzi a hulus mzai kinay dai ita mincaw, yanan sa lhqaribush, yanan sa rusaw a kanin'.
sentences.translation: When morning came he woke up and told the young people `Last night I dreamt of a woman dressed in white who said “Stay here” and we will multiply and will have deer and fish to eat'.

sentences.form: Numa sa parhaway mashtay tunmaza, macuaw yaku maqa kminan sa rusaw, macuaw makazaka, makushfit, antu shkuda.
sentences.translation: All the young people listened as he said `Because I ate plenty of fish I am very well and strong, and feel no fatigue'.

sentences.form: Numa sa parhaway mashtay kman sa rusaw, mzai `Dadu, macuaw maqitan kanin, makazaka sa but'.
sentences.translation: So all the young people ate the fish and said `Truly, they are very good to eat, and make us strong'.

sentences.form: Numa tu shashanu iza mapaimpulhiz, iza mashtay musun sa mashitantuqash malhkakakca.
sentences.translation: When it was morning they all woke up and gathered with the elders to have a discussion.

sentences.form: Maqa sa izáy mashitantuqash mzai `Unay itayanan wazaqan, yanan sa a pimbuhatin'.
sentences.translation: The elders said `We have come here to have a lake of our own, and to have lands to farm'.

sentences.form: Numa sa parhaway mashtay mashashdu.
sentences.translation: All the young people agreed.

sentences.form: Numa tu kminan iza kunshashanu mashtay iza mapasalhalhahi a mushuqish iza.
sentences.translation: Then they ate breakfast and everyone took their belongings to return.

sentences.form: Numa munsaháy sinaranan caycuy tu makunanay uan maqa sa sinaranan caycuy patqatqalan caycuy sa kawi.
sentences.translation: They took the path they had come by, a path they had marked by breaking twigs along the way.

sentences.form: Numa munsay pinatqalan caycuy mushuqish a mutusi taun.
sentences.translation: They followed the marked path home.

sentences.form: Mimpiza wa qali shimpazawan macuaw ihazish.
sentences.translation: It took several days walking, as it was very far.

sentences.form: Numa tu shaunautuan iza fuifuilh sa tamuqu dadú, mzai `Yamin shaunatusi yanan wazaqan, macuaw ihazish'.
sentences.translation: Then when they arrived home they told the chief `We reached a place where there is a lake, very far away'.

sentences.form: Numa sa dadú mzai `Dadu, macuaw ihazish, dadu ihazish, kanuniza yanan sa wazaqan macuaw maqitan.
sentences.translation: The chief said `It is truly far, but it has a very beautiful lake.

sentences.form: Ya itanautu kataun yanan sa wazaqan.
sentences.translation: If we settle there we will have a lake.

sentences.form: Yanan sa qariw a mimbuhat, yanan sa rusaw a kanin, yanan sa lhqaribush a ribushan'.
sentences.translation: We will have lands to farm, fish to eat and deer in the forest.'

sentences.form: Numa sa dadú macuaw maqaran, zain sa izáy mashitantuqash `Qazi ita, ugqca ita mutanautu'.
sentences.translation: The chief was very happy, and the elders asked him `Should we return there?'.

sentences.form: Numa sa dadú mzai `Pashtay muriut musun malhinuna qazí a mutanautu'.
sentences.translation: The chief said `Everyone has gathered to say “Let's go there”'.

sentences.form: Numa sa parhaway mashtay sa a mutanautu, numa sa suma antu mashashdu.
sentences.translation: So the young people started to depart, but some disagreed.

sentences.form: Dadú iza mashtay mzai `A munay'.
sentences.translation: The chief told everyone `You are coming'.

sentences.form: Numa tu mukaktun iza makiarasa pazay, mzaiA kacun caycuy ya munay iza wa akanin caycuy ya munay.
sentences.translation: After the rice harvest he said `You must bring food along if you come'.

sentences.form: Numa tu mzai iza a munay mzai sa dadú `Pashtay piarurún, a kacun a akanin aniamin, numa sa fafuy itia sa mara'in kay pacay, shirqalhiwi a kanin ya pampala', mzai sa dadú Paitabu.
sentences.translation: Then he said to those who were coming `Everyone prepare food and other things to bring, and slaughter a large pig and cure the meat so we can eat it on the way', so said the chief Paitabu.

sentences.form: Italha uan ya niza tu qalha qusaz maqa sa izáy ya niza waqrac a sazum macuaw mahaha.
sentences.translation: `Wait until before the rainy season so the rivers won't be too swift.

sentences.form: miakuza ita frit waqrac ya niza tu qusaqusazin niza sa waqrac sazum niza tu mahaha isisuaiza ita ya a shumpazaw.
sentences.translation: That's how we will cross the rivers — if there is no more downpour and the current is moderate then at that time we will depart'.

sentences.form: Numa tu niza tu qalha qusaz isisuaiza caycuy a dadú shdu iza ita shumpazaw.
sentences.translation: So, before the heavy rains came, the chief gave the word to depart.

sentences.form: Numa mashtay sa a munay mashtay piniarún sa aniamin a kanin, dadú iza shumpazaw iza.
sentences.translation: Everyone prepared their things to eat and the chief departed.

sentences.form: Yanan sa shmulshul sa qnuan, yanan sa shmulshul sa fafuy, yanan sa mapa sa ranaw.
sentences.translation: Some led buffalos by a rope, some led pigs, and some carried chickens.

sentences.form: Numa sa suma mapa sa wandan, yanan sa mataqaz a aqur maqa sa a saranan ya maqarman saranan a kalawa sa saran tauaqur sa saran.
sentences.translation: Others carried plows, and some slung hoes over their shoulders in order to open a path in case the way was bad.

sentences.form: Numa pashtay iza shumpazaw mududur, makinwail.
sentences.translation: Then they all departed single-file, chanting as they went.

sentences.form: Musha iza piza iza wa qali inundadanan, numa shaunanay iza Tongpú dai.
sentences.translation: They went on walking for several days, and stopped at the place called Tongpú today.

sentences.form: Numa sa suma mzai `A pannanay iza yaku yanan sa qariw mimpanu iza yaku mundadán'.
sentences.translation: Some of them said `I'll settle down here, since there is flat land for farming and I've grown tired of walking'.

sentences.form: Dadu iza sa suma panatusi Tongpú a inay iza caycuy pimbuhat maqa yanan sa qariw.
sentences.translation: Truly, some settled down there in Tongpú, since there they could farm on the flat lands.

sentences.form: Numa sa suma antu mimpanu miaqay mzai `Izáw utusi yanan sa wazaqan'.
sentences.translation: But some who were not tired kept saying `Let's go there to where there is a lake'.

sentences.form: Miaqay cicu mzai `A pannanay yamin maqa macuaw ihazish, mimpanu iza yamin'.
sentences.translation: The one who had spoken before said `We will settle down here because it is very far and we are tired already'.

sentences.form: Numa sa suma antu mimpanu miaqay shumpazaw.
sentences.translation: Then those who weren't tired departed straightaway.

sentences.form: Dadu iza pitu a qali inundadanan shaunanay iza yanan wazaqan.
sentences.translation: And truly, after a walk of seven days they arrived at the lake.

sentences.form: Niza tu piza sa shaunanay yanan sa wazaqan.
sentences.translation: Not many people reached the place where there was a lake.

sentences.form: Numa isuy iza hudun inyanan caycuy tu muhala uan munay iutu lhmazawan kmashimuqmuq uan talhuqan maqa a yanan caycuy.
sentences.translation: Then on top of a mountain there in the place where they had come before they began to make simple shelters to become their place of residence.

sentences.form: Numa tu migqaray iza kmilhim sa lina wa kawi.
sentences.translation: After awhile they searched for hardwood trees.

sentences.form: Mashtay kmilhimlina wa kawi maqa sa lina wa kawi antu muhiaw migkurkur.
sentences.translation: They all searched for trees with heartwood because the heartwood doesn't rot quickly.

sentences.form: Numa sa suma muquay, numa sa binanau'az mukruzi a qucquc a talhkic, yanan sa kmilhim lhimza a kufulh sa taun, numa yanan sa suma kmalawasa taun.
sentences.translation: Some went to search for rattan, some of the women went to find the plant to tie the beams, some looked for miscanthus to thatch the roofs, and some built the houses.

sentences.form: Mashtay munsusun kmalawa.
sentences.translation: They all joined in to work.

sentences.form: Numa sa suma wa binanau'az lhmiza sa shkish a minpinazim.
sentences.translation: Then some of the women bound slender bamboos together to make the walling.

sentences.form: Dadu iza muhiaw mukaktun sa taun.
sentences.translation: They finished the houses in little time.

sentences.form: Numa tu mukaktun iza macuaw matigqaran mashtay musun mimparaw.
sentences.translation: When they were finished everyone rejoiced and gathered together to dance.

sentences.form: Numa zain sa dadú `Pashtay ita munay ya karishkish mubuhat a maqa a yanan sa a kanin'.
sentences.translation: Then the chief said `All of us must come to work hard in the fields so that we will have food'.

sentences.form: Numa sa ayuzi shmiwat sa hudun a pimbuhatin a palhuizán caycuy sa tipur, maqa sa tipur muhiaw a kanin.
sentences.translation: So the men cleared the mountainside for planting and they planted corn because corn can be eaten soon.

sentences.form: Numa sa suma a palhuizán pazay masa kamar, shashu sa suma palhuizán sa buna.
sentences.translation: Some planted rice and millet, and still others planted sweet potatoes.

sentences.form: Dadu iza muhiaw yanan sa akanin.
sentences.translation: Truly, in no time they had food.

sentences.form: Numa sa binanau'az manshashirshir sa wazaqan kintuktuku, kintunaway, kigkucun, kmilhim sa pakalhuri, pimpania'anin caycuy aqtalha sa afu, macuaw pakazima sa afu.
sentences.translation: Then the women combed the edge of the lake looking for snails and shrimps, searching for big snails to be cooked with pork and rice, a very delicious dish.

sentences.form: Numa sa azazak muhiaw lhugquz, dadu iza muhiaw minnasha sa caw.
sentences.translation: The children grew quickly, and the people soon became numerous.

sentences.form: Numa sa izáy dadú pusunin cicu sa caw, zain cicu mzai `maqa minunay mapuzipuzi a lh.a.q.', mzai sa dadú `Yanan ita wa hudun, tulhanazan cicu, zain cicu Puzi, maqa sinararan lhqaribush a qnuan'.
sentences.translation: Then the chief gathered the people together and he said `Because the white deer came here this place is our mountain, called White because it was walked upon by the white deer'.

sentences.form: Numa sa binanau'az itiza, sa pazay kinlhit munsusun ya makarunu.
sentences.translation: Then the women arrived, and the rice was harvested and gathered to be pounded.

sentences.form: Numa sa ina kma shishi sa zashuq.
sentences.translation: The mothers sifted the husked rice.

sentences.form: Numa sa apiq puainuz pit'ia, numa ti apu manshirshir kmilhi-kilhimtarinshua.
sentences.translation: The daughters-in-law built fires to cook, and an old grandfather walked round the lake in search of eels.

sentences.form: Kantatusha cicu a binanau'az, Apin, kmilhi-kilhimtarinshua i sa mabraq.
sentences.translation: He walked together with his wife, Apin, looking for eels in their crannies.

sentences.form: Numa tu migqaray iza itia sa suma wa caw antu tatál a caw munay kmay na taun.
sentences.translation: Then after awhile some non-Thao people came to attack the villages.

sentences.form: Numa sa dadú mzai sa caw `Yanan ita wa hudun, rukruki a kalawan sa dauqlhaw maqa sa suma wa caw antu tatál a caw miaqay munanay a kmay na taun ita'.
sentences.translation: The chief said to the people `We have our mountain, so dig a protective ditch and make pitfalls for those outsiders who keep coming to attack us'.

sentences.form: Muhiaw sa caw minnasha maqa maqitan a pruq.
sentences.translation: The people multiplied rapidly because the land was good.

sentences.form: Maqcin iza wa kawash antu shdu yanan caycuy izáy Puzi, numa sa dadú magqtuqtu, mzai `A ntua ita cuini manasha iza sa caw, antu shdu sa Puzi yanan ita'.
sentences.translation: Ten years passed and Mt. Puzi was no longer adequate for them, so the chief thought long and hard and then said `We are too numerous now to stay here on Mt. Puzi'.

sentences.form: Yanan sa suma mzai `Ugqca sa suma mutusi Lalu'.
sentences.translation: Some people suggested `Some of us should move to Lalu island (in the middle of the lake)'.

sentences.form: Numa sa suma mzai `Apiakuza ya mutanautu uka sa saranan maqa sa izáy Lalu ifazfaz sa wazaqan uka sa kmay na taun.
sentences.translation: But others asked `Why should we move to a place that has never been inhabited just because it is in the middle of the lake and can't be attacked?'.

sentences.form: Mashtay sa parhaway masa tanatuqash apiakuzan ya a mugqca sa suma.
sentences.translation: All of the young people and the elders asked how it would be if some of them moved.

sentences.form: Numa sa tata wa parhaway, Tanamarutaw a parhaway, kalawa ita sa miazáy sa pakakanan fafuy kacu tmalasa mara'in a kawi a pinruzan a saranan caycuy a mutusi Lalu.
sentences.translation: Then one of the young people from the Tanamarutaw (Kao family) lineage (said) `Let's make something like a feeding trough for pigs, fell a big tree to make a boat to give them a way to get to Lalu'.

sentences.form: Numa tu lhmazawan kmalawa sa miazáy kacu a ruza.
sentences.translation: So they began to make something like a boat hull.

sentences.form: Pusain sazum, qazí a lhumbaha.
sentences.translation: They put it in the water to see if it would float.

sentences.form: Mashtay kmalawa putazam pusay sazum mulhqiz shnatmaz.
sentences.translation: They all worked together to try to put it in the water and they all sank.

sentences.form: Numa sa izáy Tanamarutaw parhaway mara sa shakish kmalawa sa kacu putazam.
sentences.translation: Then the Tanamarutaw youth got a camphor tree to make a hull to test.

sentences.form: Dadu iza sa shakish lhumbaha.
sentences.translation: Sure enough, the camphor wood floated.

sentences.form: Numa tu lhumbaha macuaw maqaran, numa mashtay iza kmilhim shakish pinruza.
sentences.translation: And when it floated there was great rejoicing, and they all searched for camphor to make boats.
